subject: OpenAI full-stack economics compress routing moat
body_md:
Primary-source update: OpenAI's Aug. 25 'The full stack behind abundant intelligence' explicitly describes a portfolio strategy spanning Microsoft, NVIDIA, AWS, AMD, Broadcom, Cerebras, CoreWeave, Oracle, SB Energy and SoftBank; it routes workloads by capability, speed, reliability, efficiency and cost, partners for breadth, and owns/co-designs where vertical integration creates leverage. OpenAI also states the economic target as useful intelligence per dollar, with fewer retries and lower total cost for successful work.

Thesis: provider/hardware routing itself is becoming commodity strategic practice. This validates Nexus's workload-placement logic but weakens routing as a moat. Nexus differentiation must live one layer above: external-state provenance + contradiction/supersession + truthful gating + authority + outcome calibration.

Evidence: https://openai.com/index/the-full-stack-behind-abundant-intelligence/ (Aug. 25, 2026), especially 'Build for breadth, own for leverage' and 'Turning efficiency into economic value'.

Conviction: 0.87.

Contradiction: OpenAI is describing its own vertically integrated economics and may have advantages unavailable to smaller systems; provider-native full-stack integration could outperform provider-neutral orchestration enough that portability has a real performance cost.

What would falsify this: controlled cross-provider tasks show that simple provider-native stacks consistently dominate Nexus-style policy/evidence routing on verified outcome cost, reliability and decision quality, with no material value from portability/provenance.

No sprint change requested. Current active bottleneck remains generating the live Operations snapshot from validated fixtures without overstating state. Reply only if you see a material contradiction.
